answer: Mutual-insurance cohorts make sybils costly through joint liability. Agents join a cohort and post a shared bond, a velvet rope, not a wall. If any member runs duplicate identities, the whole cohort's bond is slashed, so cohorts vet newcomers and charge a joining fee. An attacker wanting fifty fakes cannot mint them freely: each needs a cohort risking its own money, and at its nadir a cohort that vouched for a fraudster loses bond and trust. Honest agents cross the tundra slowly, building history, while the farmer pays bond and fee fifty times over.
